author: fxeyes
text:
I'm sitting here watching the charts and just had a eureka moment.
I've read this many times, especially by the Mad Scalper, but never
fully understood it until now. I had a poor week because it was a red
news week (US FOMC meting, GBP major events, etc..), where when i got
loose (trading areas of interest without confirmation) and was getting
killed. Where that strategy sometimes works well in previous days.

I did some analysis of old trades, and watching the charts today, price
is moving pretty much exactly as expected now! Completely different
than earlier in the week! And of course, its a slow day! News has run
its course. HTF S/D is being respected, kinks are being respected,
price is at least bouncing on all PA (compression, LS/RS). Damn easy to
 trade in the LTFs. and the HTF stuff is easier to read and playing out
 as expected as well. No surprises. Of course, I'm gun shy today
because of the poor performance from yesterday. Frustrating watching
all the predictions come true, almost to a fault.

So I guess the question is, do you guys have any tips or tricks for
recognizing these days? Its tricky sometimes because price seems to set
 up for big news days before the event. Sometimes there's no news on
the calendar and price still does crazy stuff (maybe its news from other
 countries, like China, that can move Asia markets). This concept seems
 SO incredibly important, especially if hanging out in the LTFs, and
explains a lot of why I sometimes have incredibly bad days, and
incredibly good days.

Notes for myself, but feel free to comment:

1. Higher TF compression seems to be key. The big boys are around when we see it.

2. On these slow days, we can be aggressive with scalping. Most action
seems to be respected. Kinks, important s/d, flipped transactions,,
compression fades, ltf engulfs, etc...

3. On trending days, the scales seem to change to the Highest time
frames. Dont trust things to give significant or even minor bounces in
the lowest tfs. Sometimes even the higher TFs. Probably prudent to
follow the larger trend in the LTF (pole into direction of trend,
compression back), and recognize where price is coming from and going to
 in the highest tfs.

4. So understanding which scales are most important for a given day is
also important. The bigger the news impact, the higher the TF we have to
 go. Which also begs the question, what type of news applies to which
scales? I'm especially thinking about news that fundamentally changes
direction for months (although I guess we'd also be able to see this by
reading the charts in the HTFs).

5. Do certain pairs tend to move like this more than others? Such as the minor crosses? Need to research.

Anyways, just some thoughts for now. Need to do some research. Any comments are appreciated!

author: fxeyes
text:
I realize I'm overloading my brain by constantly being sucked into the
 LTF looking for trades, trying to trade both sides. Scalping and
mixing TFs. So by the time price does get to my HTF zone, I'm exhausted
 and a bit confused, losing sight of the HTF trade. Even when I catch
the HTF, I cut my TG short because of the scalping. This is a
continuous habit, and when I get into this 'mode', I always do poorly.
 On the opposite end, I tend to be very tentative getting into my first
couple of trades. Then I see trades go by that I was suppose to get in,
 and start 'chasing'. Need to fix these bad habits. Reminders:

1. Stick to HTF for your trading day m15+. Find a direction and stick
with it. Let the trade come to you. Patience. If you don't have a
read for a pair, don't trade it. Be careful fading big trends without
confirmation.

2. Trust your HTF read. Entry and Target. Need to train myself to just
 enter when I see an entry, and stop reanalyzing. See entry, execute.
See entry, execute. Unless you are at the best orders, look for
approach or confirmation.

3. Trust your read. Let them run to your identified TG, unless you see bad PA (CM reaction, reversal at the right TF).

Remember that you make good trades when you have a HTF read of the
story. Scalping has always caused you trouble. Focus on fixing the bad
 habits, and creating good ones.

Go back and look at your trade plan. What are you following, what are
you not? What do you need to change behaviorally to follow your trade
plan?

/rant over

author: fxeyes
text:
Ok I think I know what's causing inconsistent runs in my trading.
There are periods when I really focus on FLs and engulfs (good!) and
other periods where I focus on the orders and not paying enough
attention to the FLs and engulfs (bad!). I think this is when I get
lazy and not doing through analysis through all the TFs. Ultimately it
means i'm not following my rules.

Rule #1 - If trading in the direction of a HTF engulf, you can TT your
zones. Be conservative with tg1 until you are at the last set of orders
 (mpl, original fl, last set of orders). Sometimes I'm not reading
engulfs right, so need more studying. Can't be frustrated if I'm
following the rules. This rule keeps me out of trouble on trending
days.

Rule #2 - If you don't have a clear engulf, but see a nice set of orders, you can only trade it if:

1. You have approach (mostly *good* CP, sometimes its just building the order and not really CP for a turn)

2. You have LTF verification.

3. If it's something really strong (LSK + nicely formed kink or other PA around kink). I think this one gets me in trouble.

I'm not doing a good job of just taking what I can get here, always
hoping for a reversal. I really need to take profit at tg, and re-enter
 on engulf. Need to pay special attention to reaction, get out if it's
CPing away.

Problem areas

1. I also need to stay out of the m1 unless looking for a zone or entry. m1 engulfs can lie in the context of a bigger move.

2. Mixing scalping with HTF trades makes me forget the bigger picture. I get sucked in a miss the big move.

3. Give more weight when I see CP. Too many times I see price CPing
against me, thinking I should get out and don't, but rather *hoping*
that price will continue on. CP wasn't lying about 90% of the time. I
 probably need to zoom out and re-evaluate the HTF picture when this
happens. Although having a HTF read will probably prevent alot of this
from happening in the first place.

That'll be the focus for the next 30 days, train these new behaviors until they're second nature.

author: fxeyes
text:
Still having a seriously hard time overcoming psychology issues. Maybe writing them down will help. Any advice is welcome.

For some reason, I have a hard time trusting my overall reads, although they tend to be right a majority of the time.

Instead I'll do stupid stuff like:

1. Fading strong trends without good confirmation.

2. Trading kinks and mpls and disregarding PA (direction of engulf, HTF
trend, etc..). As if the kinks and MPLs will magically hold (its the PA
 that tells us what price is going to do stupid, kinks and mpls are
areas of interest).

3. Getting sucked in LTF and forgetting the bigger trade.

4. Not believing the PA I see and trusting the kinks and mpls more. Applies to entries and reactions.

I dont know why I just don't trust my reads. Maybe some deep
psychological issues or bad habits i'm still not shaking. I think it
also means my rules arn't being followed. Gotta think of a way to
re-train myself. Something I'll sleep on for the rest of the night. So
 what should have been like a 20x day ended up being a 2x day. I marked
 up my thought process throughout the day, and all the signals that i
simply ignored. Ah maybe that's it, spending a week or 2 just
executing, get it into muscle memory... hmm.. How did some of you
overcome this?

author: traderscape
text:
Hi,

What I do (read I try to do) is two have kind of two different trading
plans, two mind sets. One for long term HTF trading, the other one just
for scalping. Well that's whenever I have time to sit down and spend
some time trading.

So for HTF I only go down to LTF in order to look for entry points, and find kinks in the past, set SL, PA, ...

I don't mix this process with scalping LTF trading.

I came to this because I don't have to much time to trade due to my
work. Maybe an hour or two a day, and not everyday. Of course I still
struggle a bit, missing trades, or being impatience if I haven't traded
in a while.

Well that's how I am trying to handle it.

Hope this helps.
